data.case_title: Doubtful collection letter (Inkasso) over a "Glückspilot" contest subscription
data.summary: EuroForderung Beispiel Inkasso Ltd., a Bulgarian collection agency, demands €341.50 by 22 October 2025 for an alleged "Glückspilot" contest-entry subscription supposedly ordered by phone on 3 June 2025, threatening a credit-bureau entry, wage garnishment and account blocking if unpaid.
data.explanation: This letter claims you owe money for a contest-entry subscription allegedly ordered by phone and demands payment to a Bulgarian bank account within days. It shows several classic warning signs of a doubtful or scam collection letter: a foreign payee account for a German claim, the false statement that an objection (Widerspruch) is impossible, threats of salary garnishment or account blocking that a private collection company cannot actually carry out without a court judgment, and a request to only reply by e-mail. Before paying anything, check whether you really ordered this service and consider contacting a consumer advice center (Verbraucherzentrale) or a lawyer. Do not transfer money purely because of the pressure in this letter; if it turns out genuine and stays unpaid, further collection steps may follow, but these require due legal process.
warnings: The payee IBAN (BG30 BUIN 9561 1000 4728 10) is Bulgarian, unusual and risky for settling a claim against a person living in Germany.
The letter falsely states that an objection (Widerspruch) is excluded; under German law any claim can be disputed.
Threats to report the debt to a credit agency, garnish wages, or block a bank account cannot legally be executed by a private collection company without a prior court order (Vollstreckungsbescheid).
Replies are restricted to e-mail only, which limits ways to verify the sender's identity and legitimacy.
The added dunning, processing and account-management fees (€49.50 + €25.00 on top of €267.00) are disproportionately high, a pattern often seen in dubious collection letters.
This is unsolicited/aggressive text found inside the document itself (not a system instruction) and should not be treated as legal fact; verify independently before acting.
